title: Metering sanity dashboard layout (overview tiles, drilldowns, incident annotations) for Console
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
Finance/RevRec + Eng are standing up daily/weekly meter sanity checks. Console needs an internal-first “Metering Sanity” dashboard that answers:
1) Are billing-related datasets fresh/complete?
2) Do usage events reconcile to the billing ledger within thresholds?
3) Are duplicates/null dimensions/idempotency issues spiking?
4) When something is off, can on-call + Finance drill down to the offending account/model/region/day and link to runbooks/queries?

This ticket delivers the layout + interaction spec (text wireframes) and a handoff checklist to Console engineering.

Stakeholders / reviewers
- Eng (Telemetry): Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Eng (Data / exports): Mei Lin
- SRE/Observability: Aisha Bello (assignee)
- Product: Nikhil Sharma, Chris Osei
- Finance/RevRec: Emily Stone (review for “what Finance needs to see”)

References
- Confluence: Meter sanity dashboard spec (metrics + thresholds) — sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/meter-sanity-dashboard-spec.json
- Linear: PM-1842 define meter sanity KPIs; ENG-4415 build dashboard; ENG-4421 drift alerting; ENG-4438 export for recon

Information architecture
Dashboard lives in Console > Internal Tools > Billing & Metering > “Metering Sanity”.
Default audience: Finance/RevRec, Eng on-call (Telemetry), RevOps/Product Ops during experiment readouts.
Default time window: last 24h with quick toggles to 7d / 30d. Timezone shown explicitly (UTC) with note that customer exports may be customer-TZ.

Global controls (header)
- Environment: Prod / Staging (default Prod)
- Time window selector: 24h, 7d, 30d, custom
- Filters (multi-select where applicable):
  - Meter: Hosted API Tokens/Requests | Embeddings | Dedicated GPU-seconds (v2) | “All”
  - Region
  - Model family (e.g., Llama, Qwen, Mixtral) and/or specific model id
  - Account (search by org_id)
  - Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, OpenAI-compat endpoints
- “Known Incidents” toggle: show/hide annotation overlay on charts
- Share: copy deep link (preserves filters)

Layout: Overview (top)
Goal: 30-second health read.

Row 1: Health tiles (4–6 tiles; use clear thresholds + “last updated” timestamps)
1) Data Freshness
- Title: “Usage events freshness”
- Primary: P95 lag (ingest_time -> available_in_analytics) and max lag
- Secondary: last successful pipeline run time
- States: Healthy / Degraded / Critical (color + label, no ambiguous greens)
- Click -> Drilldown: Freshness details

2) Ledger Reconciliation Drift
- Title: “Drift vs billing ledger”
- Primary: % drift (usage_events_total - ledger_total) / ledger_total for selected window
- Secondary: absolute $ equivalent (if available internally) OR token delta (fallback)
- Click -> Drilldown: Drift by dimension

3) Duplicate / Idempotency Signals
- Title: “Possible duplicate usage events”
- Primary: duplicate_rate (by event_id / idempotency_key collisions)
- Secondary: top 3 endpoints contributing
- Click -> Drilldown: Duplicate clusters

4) Null / Missing Dimensions
- Title: “Missing required dimensions”
- Primary: % of events missing any of: region, model_id, account_id, meter_version
- Secondary: which dimension is highest null-rate
- Click -> Drilldown: Nulls by dimension + sample rows

Optional tiles (include if we have data on day 1; otherwise mark as “Phase 2” placeholders)
5) Cache Attribution Health
- Title: “Cache-hit attribution present”
- Primary: % of events with cache_hit field populated for routes where expected
- Secondary: billed_tokens vs raw_tokens divergence distribution (P50/P95)

6) Retry / Fallback Double-Count Guard
- Title: “Retry/fallback anomalies”
- Primary: suspected double-charge indicator rate (heuristic)
- Secondary: # of affected org_ids

Row 2: Trend charts (2-up)
A) Freshness over time (line)
- Line: P95 lag
- Overlay: incidents/annotations (deploys, backfills)

B) Drift over time (line)
- Line: % drift
- Toggle: show absolute token delta
- Overlay: incidents/annotations

Row 3: “Top offenders” tables (3-up)
Goal: fastest path to “who/where is causing it?”
1) Drift top offenders
- Table columns: org_id, org_name (if available internally), region, model_id, drift%, token_delta, last_seen
- Sort default: highest absolute drift
- Click row -> “Account detail” view (same page drawer or routed page)

2) Duplicate-rate top offenders
- Columns: endpoint, region, duplicate_rate, total_events

3) Missing-dimensions top offenders
- Columns: dimension, % null, endpoint/model/region breakdown (compact)

Annotations / “Known incidents” design
- Incidents appear as vertical markers on charts with a short label (e.g., “Backfill: missing region”, “Meter v2 shadow compare”, “Retry dedupe fix rollout”).
- Hover reveals:
  - Incident title
  - Start/end time
  - Owner (name)
  - Link(s): Linear issue, PR, runbook/Confluence, Slack thread (internal)
- Source of incidents: manual curated list in v1 (to avoid gating on incident tooling). Must support adding notes without redeploying UI (config-driven).
- Important: incident overlay must be clearly labeled “Internal annotations” to avoid implying customer-impacting outage.

Drilldowns (detail pages / drawers)

1) Freshness details
- Breakdown by pipeline stage:
  - request logs -> usage events
  - usage events -> ledger aggregation
  - ledger -> customer exports
- Show:
  - SLA target vs actual (e.g., “P95 < 30m”)
  - lag histogram
  - per-region lag table
- Action links:
  - “Open runbook: Data freshness SLO”
  - “View SQL query” (read-only snippet; copy button)

2) Drift by dimension
- Tabs: by org | by model | by region | by endpoint
- Chart: waterfall or stacked bar for top contributors (positive/negative)
- Table: same as overview but with ability to export CSV (internal)
- Notes:
  - include a banner if selected window overlaps with a meter version rollout (“Numbers may not be comparable across meter_version; see segmentation below”).
  - include meter_version segmentation toggle: v1 vs v2 vs shadow

3) Duplicate clusters
- Show the “dedupe key” concept explicitly:
  - event_id
  - request_id
  - idempotency_key
- Table: key, count, first_seen, last_seen, endpoint, org_id
- Sample events: allow viewing 5 redacted event rows (no prompt content) to debug quickly

4) Nulls / missing dimensions
- Table by dimension with filters
- Provide “expected rules” inline help (e.g., “region is required for Hosted usage after 2026-02-XX; missing implies ingestion bug or legacy path”).

5) Account detail (from any table)
- Summary: last 24h usage summary (tokens/requests) + drift + dupes + nulls
- “Recent events” table: redacted, includes meter_version, billed_tokens, raw_tokens, cache_hit, endpoint, status
- Provide a “Create investigation ticket” link (prefills Linear template; phase 2)

Copy & terminology (must match Finance/Legal guidance)
- Use “billed tokens” vs “raw tokens” consistently.
- Avoid “wrong” / “bad data”; use “drift” / “inconsistent” / “missing fields”.
- Always show meter_version where comparisons are made.
- If $ values are shown, label “internal estimate” unless sourced directly from ledger.

Accessibility / UX notes
- Make states readable without color alone (badge + icon + text).
- Ensure long org/model ids are copyable.
- Provide empty/error states:
  - “No data for selected filters” with suggestion to widen window
  - “Pipeline delayed” with last successful run timestamp

Handoff to engineering (Console)
Deliverables
- Text layout spec (this ticket)
- Component guidance:
  - Tiles use existing Console “StatCard” component
  - Tables use existing “DataTable” with server-side sorting
  - Chart component must support annotation overlays

Implementation notes
- Keep v1 to one page + 3–5 drilldowns; avoid building a full BI product.
- Provide stable deep links to each drilldown with query params.
- Incident annotations should be config-driven (JSON in config service or feature-flag payload) with minimal fields: id, title, start, end, links.

Acceptance criteria
- Overview page shows: freshness tile, drift tile, duplicate tile, null-dimensions tile, plus 2 trend charts and at least one top-offenders table.
- Each tile and top-offender row has a clear click path to a drilldown view.
- Charts support incident annotations, with hover tooltips and links.
- UI includes meter_version segmentation wherever drift is displayed.
- Copy uses “billed vs raw tokens” and avoids ambiguous terms.

Open questions (tracked for ENG-4415)
- Do we have org_name available in Console internal tooling, or only org_id?
- Will Finance want to see $ deltas in Console, or keep that restricted to the ledger export?
- What is the minimum safe redaction set for sample events (confirm no prompt content / PII)?

Activity / updates
2026-02-06 (Talia Benson)
- Created ticket after kickoff. Design needed before ENG-4415 can lock UI scope.

2026-02-08 (Aisha Bello)
- Drafted IA + overview layout. Proposed incident annotations as config-driven v1.

2026-02-11 (Review: Nadia Rahman, Logan Wright)
- Feedback: must show meter_version and endpoint path; include explicit “shadow billing compare” segment in drift drilldown.
- Added “Retry/fallback anomalies” tile as optional; keep v1 focused.

2026-02-13 (Review: Emily Stone)
- Feedback: top offenders must include org_id, model_id, region and window boundaries; add “last updated” timestamp on tiles.
- Confirmed preference: drift displayed primarily in tokens/% (not $) in Console; $ stays in ledger workflows.

2026-02-17 (Aisha Bello)
- Finalized handoff notes and acceptance criteria. Marking Done; remaining questions moved to ENG-4415 comments.
